can.boots: Jag kan ta på mig stövlarna
can.bake: Jag kan hjälpa till att baka
can.umbrella: Jag kan fälla upp ett paraply

englishSourceNotes: 'I can draw a picture' sits in the same school domain as the shipped 'I can paint a picture' — near-duplicate on one sheet. Swedish separates them (rita med kritor / måla en bild), tied to the crayon cue; consider 'I can draw with crayons' in EN too.
'My favorite bug' offers snail, spider and worm, which are not bugs/insects; fine colloquially for 5-year-olds, but 'creepy-crawly' is the accurate umbrella (Swedish 'kryp' covers all nine).
'My favorite treat' pools sweets with pancake, waffle and muffin, and pancake + muffin also appear under 'My favorite breakfast' — the same picture can answer two different questions.
'My favorite clothes' (plural) above a single-picture choice; 'My favorite thing to wear' reads more naturally.
'I can help bake a cake' — the baking cue picture shows a chef with pizza/bread-like food, not a cake; Swedish drops 'a cake' ('hjälpa till att baka').
'I can catch a fish' is a big claim for a 5-year-old; the fishing-rod cue fits 'I can go fishing' better.
'I can walk a long way' with the hiking cue is fine; 'I can go for a long walk' is slightly more childlike.

optionWordFlags.problem: The picture is an adult hen (comb, wattle); 'kyckling' means chick (and chicken meat). Should be 'höna'.
'kappa' reads as a woman's dress coat; a child calls this 'jacka' (or 'rock'). The 'I can' sentence uses 'jackan' for this reason.

Verbs (infinitives) mixed in one row with nouns (fotboll, simning, skridskoåkning, skidåkning, schack). Consistent nouns would be cykling, fiske, målning, läsning, sång — or all verbs. Children can cope, but the row reads uneven.
14 letters — very long to copy for a förskoleklass child next to 'tennis'; 'åka skridskor' or 'skridskor' is easier.
Word is right, but the picture is one large red round cherry that looks like the apple in the same row — children may circle the wrong one.
Same picture/word also offered under treat — a child sees 'muffins' on two rows of the set.

otherNotes: pet heading is 'Mitt favorithusdjur', not 'Mitt favoritdjur' — the latter is already the shipped 'animal' heading and would print twice across the set.
Genus checked: frukt/grönsak/hobby/sötsak/fågel/frukost/form = en (Min); husdjur/instrument/kryp/havsdjur/fordon/gårdsdjur = ett (Mitt); kläder plural (Mina).
treat: 'godis' was rejected because the row holds cake, pancake and waffle; 'efterrätt' rejected because of lollipop and cookie. 'sötsak' covers the whole row.
Only 'Mitt favoritinstrument' (22) reaches the target limit; everything else is 15-21 characters.
All 'Jag kan' sentences follow the shipped pattern (no final full stop, definite body-part/garment: håret, händerna, jackan, stövlarna, sängen), 13-29 characters.
skip (shipped 'hoppa hopprep') and puddle ('hoppa i vattenpölar') both use 'hoppa' but mean clearly different things; acceptable.
Picture 'activities/hiking' also shows walking poles — 'vandra' fits; 'fish' cue is a fishing rod: 'meta' would be the most exact child verb, but 'fånga en fisk' keeps the English meaning.

Follow-up 2026-09-27: tidy/coat/swing/draw revised per the US panel. bake kept ('Jag kan hjälpa till att baka' fits a whisk cue). draw is 31 characters (under the hard max of 34); 'färglägga' keeps it apart from the shipped 'måla en bild'.
